subject: Post-call readout: BioQuest inference capacity — isolation & reservation path
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Emily Chen <emily.chen@bioquest.com>, Jason Park <jason.park@bioquest.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call readout: BioQuest inference capacity — isolation & reservation path

Thanks Emily & Jason — great conversation this morning. Below is a concise readout (high level + immediate next steps) so your team has a single artifact to share internally. I captured the technical/ops asks we discussed and a recommended reservation path.

Summary of what we heard (pain & goals)
- Primary workload: clinical triage model (PHI) + nightly batch scoring for retrospective studies.
- Main pain: unpredictable latency during peak inference windows (multi-tenant interference) and difficulty meeting internal SLA of p95 < 150ms for real-time triage.
- Compliance constraints: PHI must be isolated or encrypted-in-use; procurement will need SOC 2 evidence and KMS/HSM support.
- Scale behavior: steady 100–300 concurrent requests most of the day with spikes to ~1,200 concurrent during morning triage and nightly batch jobs that use sustained throughput for 2–3 hours.

Redwood recommendation (reserved-dedicated path)
1) Short-term (pilot, weeks 0–4): 4x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs in a private pool (customer-isolated tenancy). This meets latency targets for current load and isolates PHI.
2) Canary & autoscaling (weeks 4–8): Add burst policy: allow automatic, policy-driven burst to shared capacity up to 8x GPUs for peak windows. Keep dedicated pool for steady traffic.
3) Long-term (production): 8x reserved GPUs with autoscale buffer + KV-prefix caching for low-latency repeated prompts. SLA target: 99.9% availability with p95 latency guardrails (we propose p95 < 150ms for short sequences; can provide a tailored SLO after one-week pilot).

Operational asks / open questions from BioQuest (applied to scope and procurement)
- Isolated tenancy required for PHI: yes (we recommended private pool).
- Data residency / retention: confirm retention window and deletion policy (you mentioned 7 years for auditability — can you confirm?).
- KMS: which provider do you use for CME / key management? We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-managed HSMs.

Attachments: scoping sheet and a first-pass MOP draft attached. I included a short cost stub (estimate) in the CSV for procurement to review.

Immediate next steps (agreements)
- Emily: confirm retention window and which KMS you want us to validate (reply by Thu, May 14).
- BioQuest procurement: if you can share the procurement cadence (timeline + PO contact), we’ll produce a formal quote and draft contract within 2 business days of confirmation of GPU sizing.
- Marcus / Redwood: schedule a 45-min dedicated-console demo for your infra and security leads next week (Rishi and Laura to join).

If helpful I can convert the recommendation into a one-page SLO & cost card for your leadership.

Thanks — Marcus

Marcus Lin
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call readout: BioQuest inference capacity — isolation & reservation path

Marcus — thanks for the summary and quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Retention: correct that clinical audit requires longer retention, but for inference logs we need a 2-year standard retention with the option to escalate records to 7 years on a per-study basis. Can Redwood support tiered retention?
2) KMS: we use AWS KMS for keys today; for certain studies compliance requires a customer-managed key stored in a separate HSM. Would you list any differences in the operational runbook for customer-managed HSM versus standard AWS KMS?
3) SLA / Sizing: the proposed 4x A100 pilot sounds reasonable for proving latency. Procurement will want a cost ballpark and a short description of cancellation terms. They also asked whether we can contractually pin model versions for the pilot.

Procurement timeline: we are targeting a June 15 PO issuance if scoping and pricing look aligned.

Next steps on our side: I’ll confirm retention window and circle back with procurement with your estimate. Also looping Jason (infra) who will coordinate with Rishi on the demo.

—Emily
Dr. Emily Chen
VP Clinical AI
BioQuest Therapeutics

Appreciate the quick reply, Emily. A few concrete items to unblock procurement and infra: 

- Tiered retention: yes — Redwood supports object retention tiers. We’ll include options in the quote (2-year standard + 7-year archival retention per-study). I’ll flag the runbook differences for HSM (short summary below).
- KMS/HSM ops difference (high level):
  * AWS KMS (standard): Redwood integrates via customer AWS IAM roles; key usage is audited and keys remain in your account. Simpler onboarding, lower ops overhead.
  * Customer-managed HSM: requires coordination on network-level access and a brief HSM attestation exchange; onboarding typically adds ~5 business days for validation and policy checks. We’ll include the additional validation step in the MOP.
- Model pinning: yes, you can pin model version for the duration of the pilot — we’ll add a version-lock clause in the pilot SOW.
- Cancellation terms: 30-day notice on reserved pools for pilot commitments (we’ll surface an exact line in the quote).

Attached: dedicated-estimate-8xA100.csv (ballpark monthly commitment + burst assumptions). We scoped two commitment bands: Pilot 4x reserved + burst to 8x (cost stub A), or Immediate 8x reserved (cost stub B).

Availability for demo: I can run a focused 45-min session on Wed, May 20 at 10:00 AM PT or Thu, May 21 at 2:00 PM PT. Rishi & Laura — which slot works for you?

Thanks — Marcus

- Canary plan (draft):
  1) Week 0: provision 4x reserved GPUs in private pool; run synthetic load to validate p95 latency < 150ms for target sequences.
  2) Week 1: integrate KV-prefix caching + run replay on last 48h of traffic (sanitized sample).
  3) Week 2: staged roll to 8x burst for 3 morning triage windows; validate throughput and fallback behavior.
  4) Week 3: finalize SLO language for SOW and prepare post-pilot regression eval.
